prompt: Write 5 short claim log entries by an auto insurance adjuster for a rear-end collision claim. Injury: whiplash. The claimant is represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1026; do not mention it.)
text:
Entry 1: Claim opened following a rear-end collision at a signalized intersection. Insured vehicle reports being struck from behind while stopped. Police report requested. Insured reports neck pain and stiffness and has seen an urgent care provider. Photos of both vehicles received and added to file.

Entry 2: Claimant has retained counsel. Letter of representation received from claimant's attorney's office requesting that all further contact be directed to counsel. Direct contact with claimant discontinued. Preliminary liability appears clear based on the other driver's admission at the scene and the physical damage pattern.

Entry 3: Medical records requested from urgent care facility and treating chiropractor through claimant's counsel. Authorization forms sent. Counsel indicates treatment is ongoing with diagnosis of cervical strain consistent with whiplash. Reviewing prior claims history for the claimant as part of standard investigation.

Entry 4: Vehicle appraisal completed for the claimant's vehicle. Repair estimate received from the preferred shop and reviewed. Rental coverage confirmed under the at-fault party's policy. Counsel requested a demand package be prepared once treatment concludes. No settlement discussions have taken place at this time.

Entry 5: Follow-up with claimant's counsel regarding outstanding medical bills and wage documentation. Counsel confirmed records are being gathered and will be forwarded. File flagged for supervisor review due to attorney involvement and ongoing treatment. Next diary set for follow-up with counsel's office.
